title: GPS Trilateration Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Turn satellites on one at a time and watch the possible positions collapse, then break the receiver clock and discover why three satellites are not enough.

learningObjectives: Explain how distances from known satellites determine a position.
Explain why four satellites are required rather than three.
prerequisites: Knowing that light travels at a finite, known speed
Reading a distance off a scale

keyQuestions: Why does the receiver not simply carry an accurate clock?
What is the same about all four range errors when the receiver clock is wrong?
Why does a receiver at the bottom of a narrow street do badly?
commonMisconceptions: Believing satellites track the receiver, rather than the receiver listening passively.
Assuming the fourth satellite is for redundancy or accuracy rather than for the clock.
Thinking more satellites always helps more than better-placed ones.
assessmentOpportunities: Explains what each additional satellite rules out.
States why the receiver clock is an unknown rather than a known.
Connects satellite spread to position accuracy without using the phrase dilution of precision.
